population: Every AMD development configuration in the frozen design-study safety corpus: 67 configurations (43 safe, 24 seeded hazardous); gfx942 18, gfx950 9, gfx1250 40. These are configurations, not 67 distinct algorithms or new application bugs.
scope: Identical ordinary full-trace CLI options in both arms; no early-readiness or memory-conflict option is enabled by this comparison. Complete historical source modules, selected-workgroup contracts, output coordinates and mathematical specifications are preserved. No heldouts are executed or used as prospective validation/tuning evidence.
qualification: One full analysis per configuration per arm; every safe configuration also receives complete output export and verify --sample 0. Unsupported, UNKNOWN, timeout, crash and an aborted graph with a property FAIL do not count as intended detections. All functional outcomes remain in the denominator.
timing_eligibility: Determined only by baseline qualification. A safe case needs complete graph/output/specification checks; a hazard needs a complete intended typed rejection. A candidate failure never filters a baseline-qualified case. New candidate-only support has absolute functional observations and no speedup ratio.
order: One separate first-observation round, followed by 31 repeated fresh-process rounds. Seeded shuffled case order; each pair runs adjacent with seeded randomized arm order. Timing starts after unrelated builds/tests stop. Record machine load; no machine-cold cache or CPU-isolation claim.
endpoints: Hazard: parent-observed first independently validated expected-property diagnostic. Safe: parent-observed process completion without optional expression export; full output/specification controls are untimed. Record process wall time, CPU time, peak RSS, return status and censored durations separately.
statistics: Per-case repeated medians and nearest-rank p95, with first observations separate. A ratio requires all 31 successful repeats in each arm. Retain every miss, timeout and regression; no outlier removal, adaptive retry, selective kernel replacement or promised improvement.
publication: Publish all per-case results and sanitized numerical samples after an independent audit. Keep raw machine identities, commands and logs outside the repository. Historical datasets remain unchanged. Synthetic mixed-wait/private controls are separate prospective coverage controls, never additional real application bugs.
